name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
summary: A voluntary US framework organizing AI risk management into four functions — Govern, Map, Measure, Manage — used widely as a baseline for enterprise AI governance programs regardless of vendor.

source.title: AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
source.reference: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).

name: EU AI Act Risk Tiering
summary: Classifies AI systems into unacceptable, high, limited, and minimal risk tiers, with obligations (documentation, human oversight, conformity assessment) scaling with risk tier.

source.title: EU Artificial Intelligence Act
source.reference: European Union regulation on artificial intelligence.

name: Microsoft Responsible AI Standard
summary: Microsoft's internal governance standard — fairness, reliability & safety, privacy & security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability — applied to AI systems built on Microsoft platforms.
applies_to: AI systems built on Azure / Microsoft platforms

name: Google Cloud AI Principles
summary: Google's public commitments guiding AI development — being socially beneficial, avoiding unfair bias, being built and tested for safety, and being accountable to people.
applies_to: AI systems built on Google Cloud

name: OpenAI Usage Policies
summary: Defines prohibited uses and required safeguards (e.g. for high-risk domains) for applications built on OpenAI models and APIs.

name: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy
summary: Anthropic's public commitment to defining AI Safety Levels and the corresponding safety/security measures required before training or deploying more capable models.

name: Cloud Vendor Compliance Programs for Regulated Industries
summary: Major cloud vendors publish compliance program documentation (HIPAA eligibility, PCI-DSS, GLBA-relevant controls) identifying which specific services can be used for regulated workloads under a signed agreement (e.g. a Business Associate Agreement for HIPAA).

source.title: Compliance program documentation — cross-vendor
source.reference: Published compliance offerings documentation across Microsoft, AWS, and Google Cloud Trust Centers.
source.excerpt: Using a HIPAA- or PCI-eligible service is necessary but not sufficient — the surrounding architecture and signed agreements still have to be in place.
